difficulty.deobfuscation: Dean-Edwards packed eval() blocks statically unpacked in place (semantically identical to runtime)
difficulty.notes: The SQ login widget ships its password encoder inside a Dean-Edwards packed eval() block (td was a packer-dictionary word). The two eval() blocks were statically unpacked in place so td/cryp/__rsa are normal functions in the file (the unpacked code is exactly what the browser eval-executes). The anchor is the login/registration dispatcher _action (the 1.json answer): it binds the password via h.password=td(f), applies g.cryps and sends the GET jsonp /login request. Graded chain: _action 1 -> td (bespoke password scrambler) 0.7 -> __rsa (shared base64 primitive) 0.5; cryp (sibling scrambler for other data) 0. The single-line file does not parse with acorn, so _action is pinned by explicit offsets. Heavy game-portal analytics noise (pt.clickdata, hm.baidu, bdstatic, turing.captcha).

task_contract.anchor_definition: The login/registration dispatcher _action (captured as the 1.json answer): it assembles the request h, binds the password via the site encoder (h.password=td(f)), applies g.cryps and sends the GET jsonp /login request. td (the bespoke password scrambler producing the observed token) 0.7, __rsa (the shared base64 primitive) 0.5, and the sibling cryp encoder 0 are graded below it.

behavior_category.subtype: position-fixed random-padded scramble of password then base64
behavior_category.recompute_check: td inserts random characters; not reproducible to a fixed value (the fixed substrings 138 / 19912565 are observable in the decoded token)

near_categories.why_not: Only the scalar password field is encoded, not the whole request body.
The value is a scrambled encoding of the password input, not a UI-state encoding.

evidence: The single-line minified file does not parse with acorn, and the password encoder it dispatches to shipped inside a Dean-Edwards packed eval() block; the anchor _action is a 3778-char dispatcher reachable only by content, and its encoder/sibling helpers exist as spans only after the eval blocks were statically unpacked.
td (password) vs cryp (other data) vs the _action dispatcher are easy to confuse; large game-portal vendor noise.

provenance.label_points_to: the _action dispatcher (the anchor); col 28498 falls inside its body, near the h.password=td(f) password binding
provenance.capture_transform_detail: The original sq.login2015.js shipped the password encoder inside a Dean-Edwards packed eval() block (td was a packer-dictionary word). That block was statically unpacked IN PLACE so td/cryp appear as ordinary named functions; the unpacked text is byte-for-byte what the browser eval-executes. This is the only case whose captured file is not a verbatim on-the-wire asset; the transform is semantics-preserving and disclosed here so the localization task remains well-defined.
